t: You're looking at a statue of Robert Aske, the seventeenth-century merchant and haberdasher who served as an Alderman of London. He is remembered as a philanthropist, and that generosity is why he is commemorated in stone here. The sculptor was William Croggon, who made the figure. Take a moment to look at how Aske is shown, and think of a City merchant whose name outlived his trade through the good he did.
